findings.problem: The allowed base is Python >=3.10. A Windows venv from 3.10/3.11 ensurepip, and often a Jupyter pip install, drops setuptools/pip .pth import hooks (non-comment lines) under Lib\site-packages. setup_notebooks.ps1 treats any such file as fatal after it just created that venv, keeps $install, and refuses reuse. install_notebook_startup.ps1 walks the whole venv and fails approval_required_python_pth_review on the same files. The installer rejects the environment it is designed to install.
findings.repair: Limit the .pth gate to path entries that escape the venv/base roots (or an explicit allowlist of ensurepip/setuptools hooks). Apply the same rule in both scripts. Do not fail a stock jupyterlab/ipykernel venv.
findings.acceptance_test: On Python 3.10 or 3.11, create the venv and pip-install the pinned Jupyter set; setup must pass its .pth loop; startup Install must not return approval_required_python_pth_review on that tree.

findings.problem: Dedicated-account ReadAndExecute is Set-Acl'd only on $install after the venv, including Scripts\python.exe, already exists. Set-Acl is not a reliable propagator onto existing children. The boot task Exec.Command is that python.exe, LogonType Password, LeastPrivilege as the dedicated user. install_notebook_startup.ps1 requires trusted owners/writers on code roots but never requires the dedicated SID to have RX on the task image or app\notebook_service.py, so RegisterTask/Run can succeed and the process still get access denied.
findings.repair: Set the dedicated SID RX on $install before venv creation, or after the tree exists push the same ACE onto every child. Before RegisterTask, require effective RX for that SID on python.exe and notebook_service.py.
findings.acceptance_test: Effective-access check as the dedicated SID: read/execute $install\python\Scripts\python.exe and $install\app\notebook_service.py; only then enable/Run the task.

findings.problem: setup_notebooks.ps1 writes runtime.execution_host from $env:COMPUTERNAME (NetBIOS). startup Install requires it -ine [Net.Dns]::GetHostName() (Winsock name, often FQDN or the untruncated device name). On mismatch the child fails settings_identity_mismatch after New-LocalUser, workspace/runtime ACL writes, and private settings already exist. setup will not reuse the account, $install, or notebook-runtime.json.
findings.repair: Stamp and compare one identifier, preferably [Environment]::MachineName on both sides; if a DNS name is kept, accept it as an alias of the NetBIOS name rather than a hard inequality.
findings.acceptance_test: On a host where Dns.GetHostName() differs from COMPUTERNAME, full Install must pass the identity check and register the task; a forced mismatch must still fail closed before New-LocalUser.

findings.problem: Native() Kill()s any child still running at 120s. The jupyterlab>=4,<5 jupyter-server>=2,<3 ipykernel>=6,<8 cold install commonly exceeds that. A timeout leaves $install at runtime_preparation; the opening Test-Path $install guard blocks retry.
findings.repair: Use a longer pip-specific wait (or no kill while stdout is still progressing). On runtime_preparation failure, allow a documented resume/delete path so the next authorized run is not stuck on the leftover directory.
findings.acceptance_test: With an empty pip cache, the Jupyter install completes without Native timeout; a simulated timeout must leave a rerunnable state rather than a permanent 'directory already exists' stop.

findings.problem: Startup enumerates every local group with Get-LocalGroupMember before RegisterTask. That cmdlet throws on unresolved, Microsoft Account, or Azure AD members. Setup has already created the dedicated user and private tree. The child then writes JSON and exit 1, which in Windows PowerShell ends the calling setup session so setup's catch/finally (warning, credential Dispose) may not run; retry is still blocked by the existing account and $install.
findings.repair: Test membership only of privileged groups by well-known SID, with per-group try/catch. From the child, emit the error JSON and return/throw to the caller; call exit 1 only when the script is the process entry point.
findings.acceptance_test: On a host whose Administrators group has a Microsoft Account member, startup Install must return its JSON to setup without killing the session and without local_account_validation_failed; the new account must remain only in Users.

limits: Read-only review of tools/setup_notebooks.ps1 and tools/install_notebook_startup.ps1; no live install, ACL probe, Task Scheduler, or browser/kernel run.
notebook_service.py / notebook_runtime.py were not read; service identity, private DACL, and local-kernel checks were taken as given, including installed-Jupyter native-init.

Set-Acl child propagation, GetHostName vs COMPUTERNAME, Get-LocalGroupMember, and nested exit 1 are judged from these call sites plus documented Windows PowerShell/API behavior, not from a run on this host.
